parsed.basis: Tavush inherits Armenia's national position: no law criminalises transgender identity itself, same-sex conduct was decriminalised in 2003, but there is no anti-discrimination or clear hate-crime protection, legal gender recognition requires surgery with no non-binary recognition, and gender-affirming care is restricted. In this border province, those national gaps combine with a rural, socially conservative and military-influenced environment around Ijevan, Dilijan and border villages, where Armenian Apostolic norms and strong traditional attitudes prevail, there is no local LGBT organisation or specialised legal aid, and distance from Yerevan makes recourse slower. Frequent security and document checks linked to the Azerbaijan border increase the chance of discovery and questioning. No documented local tolerance or protective exception distinguishes Tavush.
